design_reasoning.reason: All architectural decisions are grounded in existing architecture documents (ARCHITECTURE_BACKEND.md, ARCHITECTURE_DATABASE.md, ARCHITECTURE_UI.md, ARCHITECTURE_TARGET.md). Each decision includes explicit justification and basis. Design is lean - uses CQRS pattern, Repository pattern, React Context as specified in target architecture. No unnecessary abstractions introduced. Defensive programming is explicit (e.g., backend enforces business rules, frontend provides UX feedback). All 18 architectural decisions reference specific ADRs or established patterns. Questions addressed section shows clear reasoning for each design choice with explicit basis.
design_reasoning.recommendation: No improvements needed. Design exemplifies best practices with clear architectural grounding.

workflow_changes.reason: Happy path is fully specified with 18 detailed workflow steps from login to logout. Each step identifies layers involved (Frontend, Backend, Database) and includes handshake points with explicit data shapes. Data transformations are clear at each boundary (e.g., step 3 shows query shape and return type, step 4 shows LoginResponse shape). Sequence and timing are explicit (synchronous API calls, async operations noted). Edge cases covered through acceptance criteria mapping: insufficient funds (step 13), future dates (step 13), zero amounts (step 13), session expiration (implicit in token validation). All 12 acceptance criteria from analysis map to workflow steps. No scope creep - design stays within story boundaries.
workflow_changes.recommendation: No improvements needed. Workflow is implementable and comprehensive.

interface_contracts.reason: All contracts are fully specified with complete shapes. Three API contracts defined: POST /api/auth/login (request/response shapes, status codes 200/401/400), GET /api/accounts/{accountId}/transactions (path params, auth headers, response shape, status codes 200/401/403), POST /api/accounts/{accountId}/transactions (path params, request body with validation rules, response shape, status codes 201/400/401/403/422). Three data models defined with complete schema (Accounts, Transactions, AccountSecurity) including columns, constraints, indexes. Three interaction patterns defined (client-side display, real-time balance, token auth) with rationale and behavior. Perfect 1:1 mapping between workflow steps and contracts - each handshake_point references a specific contract. Data shapes match across workflow steps (e.g., LoginResponse in step 4 matches POST /api/auth/login contract).
interface_contracts.recommendation: No improvements needed. Contracts are complete and aligned with workflow.

layer_responsibilities.reason: All responsibilities clearly assigned across Frontend (13 responsibilities), Backend (10 responsibilities), and Database (9 responsibilities). Each responsibility includes explicit intent explaining why that layer owns it (e.g., 'Frontend owns UI presentation', 'Backend owns security boundary', 'Database owns data integrity'). Boundaries are explicit - workflow handshake_points show exactly what crosses each boundary. Design follows established patterns: CQRS with MediatR (Backend), Repository pattern (Backend), React Context (Frontend), shadcn/ui (Frontend), TanStack Table (Frontend). No contradictions with existing architecture - all patterns align with ARCHITECTURE_*.md documents. Reuses existing components/utilities where applicable (shadcn/ui, TanStack Table, MediatR, Entity Framework Core). Defensive programming explicit: backend enforces business rules (insufficient funds, date validation), frontend provides UX feedback (client-side validation, error display).
layer_responsibilities.recommendation: No improvements needed. Layer responsibilities are exemplary with clear rationale.

instrumentation.reason: Five instrumentation events defined with rich context: UserLoginAttempt (username, success, timestamp, ip_address), TransactionCreated (transaction_id, source/target accounts, amount, timestamp), TransactionValidationFailed (account_id, failure_reason, requested_amount, current_balance, timestamp), TransactionListViewed (account_id, transaction_count, response_time_ms, timestamp), SessionExpired (account_id, session_duration_minutes, timestamp). At least one event per major workflow branch (login, transaction creation success/failure, transaction viewing, session management). Error states covered comprehensively (validation failures, session expiration). Performance-critical paths have timing instrumentation (response_time_ms for transaction list queries). Data transformations include validation logging (failure_reason, current_balance for context). All events include relevant context for debugging (user/account IDs, error types, performance metrics).
instrumentation.recommendation: No improvements needed. Instrumentation is comprehensive with rich context for observability.
